holidays.name: National Pigs-in-a-Blanket Day
holidays.description: Today is for little sausages wrapped in flaky pastry or fluffy dough. Serve them hot, dunk them in mustard or ketchup, and eat more than you meant to. They show up at parties, brunches and kids' tables, and they're gone within minutes.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It has become a yearly favorite on the American snack calendar.
holidays.funFact: In the United Kingdom, 'pigs in blankets' are a different dish. They are small sausages wrapped in bacon, and they are a must-have at Christmas dinner.

holidays.name: National Bucket List Day
holidays.description: This is a day to dust off your dream list and cross something off it. It might be skydiving, a trip to Iceland, or finally learning the accordion. The idea is that it's never too late to make a memory worth having.
holidays.origin: National Day Calendar created the day in collaboration with Cindy Rhodes, a bucket list coach and travel host. She pitched it as a yearly reminder to chase your biggest goals.
holidays.funFact: The phrase 'bucket list' comes from 'kicking the bucket.' It became a household term after the 2007 film The Bucket List, starring Jack Nicholson and Morgan Freeman.

holidays.name: New Kids on the Block Day
holidays.description: Fans of the 1980s and '90s boy band put on their best matching outfits, dust off the cassettes and sing along to the hits. It's a day for 'Step by Step' dance moves and teenage-crush nostalgia.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial fan observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the Boston pop group that became a worldwide sensation.
holidays.funFact: New Kids on the Block formed in Boston in 1984. Producer Maurice Starr put the group together, and it went on to sell millions of albums.
